newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan grain/oilseed buying sees little USDA impact.
newsitem.headline: Japan grain/oilseed buying sees little USDA impact.

text.p: Japanese grain and oilseed buyers said on Monday they are carefully monitoring Chicago futures after Friday's bullish USDA crop data, but do not expect it will affect their purchases with only modest buying seen this week.
"The USDA report was surprise news," an official in a major oil crusher's purchasing department said. "But we'd like to wait and see whether Chicago's rally will be sustained."
Japan has completed purchasing U.S. soybeans for February shipment and is gradually showing interest in March positions, traders said.
"Modest buying from Japan is expected to emerge this week," the oil crusher's official said.
Japanese premiums for U.S. soybeans were quoted at about 130 U.S. cents a bushel over the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) March contract, traders said.

Local traders said they have bought up to 450,000 tonnes of Brazilian soybeans so far this season, and price movements in the Chicago market will determine their next purchases from the South American crop.
In the corn market, Japanese buyers have covered nearly 10 percent of their requirements from the U.S. crop for April-June shipment.
Japanese premiums for U.S. corn were quoted at slightly below 100 U.S. cents a bushel over the CBOT May contract, traders said.

"The impact (from the USDA report) was stronger in the soybean market. We're not sure if the corn market's price gains will remain, and would like to watch," a corn trader at a major trade house said.
Some trade houses are showing interest in Argentine and Chinese corn, and price competitiveness against U.S. origin will be a key factor, they said.
Nearby freight rates from the U.S. Gulf to Japan for bulk grains were quoted at around US$26.00 a tonne.
The Food Agency, the grain trading arm of the Agriculture Ministry, said it would carry out the first weekly import tender for this year on January 16.
By the end of this month, the agency said it plans to buy about 698,000 tonnes of wheat and barley for March shipment.
"We don't expect the Chicago wheat market's price rally to change our import plans," a Food Agency official said.
